reason: Preseal editorial clarification explicitly spells out locally finite/nonnegative-integer grading and ordinary Q-operator/integer-count category. No theorem/native/source change.
old_paragraph: Fix any positive integer r and any ordinary unweighted r-differential poset P: it has one minimum, finite ranks, and the exact integer identity DU−UD = rI at every rank, including rank zero. Put pⱼ = |Pⱼ|. This is the standard ordinary category, allowing zero common covers; it is not an identity interpreted only modulo a characteristic.
new_paragraph: Fix any positive integer r and any ordinary unweighted r-differential poset P: a locally finite poset graded by the nonnegative integers, with one minimum and finite ranks. Its ordinary up and down operators over ℚ satisfy DU−UD = rI at every rank, including rank zero, as an equality of integer incidence counts. Put pⱼ = |Pⱼ|. Zero common covers are allowed; an identity interpreted only modulo a characteristic is not the category used here.
